correctness.rationale: The specified 24-vector cubic-field construction gives the regular snub cube with 32 triangular and 6 square supporting faces and 60 edges. A central generic section crosses precisely those graph edges whose endpoint signs against U are opposite. The inspected exact finite checker enumerates all vertex triples with cubic-field rational-isolator sign tests, the 24 great circles from vertices, all pair intersections, oriented local sectors and 1824 corner incidences. It derives 482 chambers with counts 6,48,108,192,72,48,8 by N=12..18. Spherical Gauss–Bonnet angle accounting yields the seven stated algebraic-angle areas and normalization 4π. Independently reconstructed all 482 chamber sign vectors numerically with identical sidedness distribution; a separate 100000-Gaussian-direction experiment had frequencies consistent with stated decimals, not used as proof. No off-center/excluded nongeneric plane classification is asserted.

value.rationale: A regular snub cube is a canonical chiral Archimedean polyhedron. The complete exact distribution of 12–18 side counts, including three positive odd outcomes, and its 482-region normal arrangement are natural stochastic-geometric invariants and genuine exact classification. Neither an ordinary static face vector nor a single mean determines this distribution.
